notes: Breadboard row letters follow the image: rows a-e (lower half) = bank 't', rows f-j (upper half) = bank 'b'. Top rail row nearer the red line = tp, nearer the blue line = tn; bottom rail row near the blue line = bn. Rail holes numbered 1-25 left to right in groups of 5.

LMV358 is a dual op-amp (LM358 pinout): 1 OUT A, 2 IN-A, 3 IN+A, 4 GND, 5 IN+B, 6 IN-B, 7 OUT B, 8 VCC. It straddles the centre gap with pins 1-4 in columns 14-17 (bank t, row e) and pins 8-5 above (bank b, row f). The notch/pin-1 orientation was inferred from the image.

The brown wire from MKR1000 A0 lands on column 14 (op-amp pin 1 = output of amplifier A); the unused second op-amp is left unconnected. The schematic draws A0 on the second op-amp's output, but the breadboard image is taken as authoritative.

Schematic mapping: R8 (100k) VCC to the signal node (pin 3), R9 (100k) signal node to GND, C1 jack signal to pin 3 node, R10 (47k) pin 2 node to GND, R11 (47k) pin 2 node to trimmer end, trimmer wiper to output (pin 1).

The trimmer's exact breadboard pins are hard to read in the image. I placed it in bank t row e, columns 1-3, with wiper in column 2, one end in column 3 (to R11) and the other end (column 1) unconnected. The purple wiper-to-output wire is drawn in the image at column 2 bank b row g; I put it on column 2 bank t (2t.d) so it shares the wiper strip, as the schematic requires.
The 3.5 mm jack is a breakout board with two blue wires. I assumed the left pad is SLEEVE (to GND rail) and the right pad is RIGHT (audio signal to C1 via column 18). The LEFT channel is unused.
Resistor positions are inferred from body positions: R10 and R11 are 47k (yellow-violet-orange); R8 and R9 are 100k (brown-black-yellow). The cap and resistor leg spacing is estimated from the image.
Software (AudioFrequencyMeter, MIDIUSB) is not part of the physical graph. The MKR1000 is powered and programmed over its micro-USB port; no cable is drawn in the image.
